_: The launch configuration for the one engine that answers everything. Committed, because the original sin here was that NO committed launch config existed anywhere: the engine serving apocky.com was traced to an EXIT trap inside a throwaway benchmark script, which a reboot would have lost silently. Every value is measured on this machine or cited; see apocrypha-core/tools/ENGINE_DIALS.csl for the evidence behind each one.

notes.-ncmoe 30: MoE experts placed on CPU. Measured +46% mean generation on the coder at -c 8192 (8.57 -> 12.50 tok/s, 3 samples each, every placed sample beat every unplaced one). The sweep 12/18/24/30/36 gave 7.35/8.13/8.36/17.44/15.97, so the knee sits between 24 and 30. N! transfer this number to another model or context.
notes.-ngl 99: Only safe BECAUSE -ncmoe is set. Alone it defeats b9743's own memory fitter: 'n_gpu_layers already set by user to 99, abort'. The -ncmoe run emits no such abort. Never remove one without the other.
notes.-c 32768 -np 2: Two slots of 16384 each, confirmed live via /slots. Two slots is what stops a long agent turn parking an interactive message behind it -- the whole point of one model serving everything.
notes.-fa on + q8_0 KV: Must move together. -fa off with quantized KV aborts outright: 'V cache quantization requires flash_attn'. The widely-cited turn-off-flash-attention-on-Arc advice is SYCL-scoped; this is Vulkan and it works.
notes.-cram 1024: The 8192 MiB default prompt cache is what turns a working engine into an OOM two minutes later on a 16 GiB card.
notes.--mlock: DELIBERATELY ABSENT. 20+ GiB of CPU-side experts against 31.8 GiB of RAM is the flag that hangs the desktop.
notes.-ncmoe 30 (re-measured at 16384): Re-swept 2026-09-16 at the LIVE context, warmed, n=6 per point: 24 = 9.07 tok/s and it trips the fitter abort; 30 = 17.31 (15.48-18.16), fixed 4475 ms; 36 = 16.42 (15.63-17.34), fixed 3228 ms. 30 and 36 are NOT separable on generation (5.4% apart, ranges overlap heavily); 36's lower fixed cost is offset by slower generation. 30 kept as the incumbent under a stopping rule declared before the sweep. The old +46% figure was measured at -c 8192 and does not transfer.
notes.WARM-UP DOMINATES THE DIALS: The same engine at identical settings gave 11.59 tok/s on its first generations and ~17.9 after a few rounds -- a ~55% climb, larger than the gap between any two -ncmoe values. Any sweep that does not warm each config first is measuring load order, not the dial: an earlier cold run understated 30 at 11.59 against a warm 18.52 baseline for the SAME config. launch-gui.js now generates 4 times before handing the engine over.
notes.-b 4096 -ub 1024 << CRASH FIX, do not r: 8192/2048 CRASHES THIS ENGINE. A tool-call prompt (~3.5k tokens, built-ins + 14 MCP tools) killed llama-server every time with GGML_ASSERT(id >= 0 && id < n_expert) at ggml-backend.cpp:1615 -- an MoE expert-routing assert, reproduced 3/3. Bisected: MCP off = survives (so it needs the big tools prompt); --cache-reuse removed = still crashes (not the cache); -ub 512 = survives; -ub 1024 = survives across 2 plain turns plus a tool-using turn, 0 asserts. Raw size alone is NOT the trigger: a 13,906-token /completion prefilled fine at -ub 2048. It is the large micro-batch meeting MoE expert offload on a tools prompt through --jinja. Cost of the fix is first-turn prefill only (~134 vs ~185 tok/s); turn 2 measured 7.3s against turn 1's 81.3s because the prefix cache carries it. ROLE: WORKING, not PROVED -- 1024 is tested, not guaranteed; drop to 512 if an assert ever returns.
